topic: Verified public dossier on Dr. Satish Kumar Regonda (Associate Professor, Civil Engineering & Climate Change, IIT Hyderabad) — identity, profiles, bibliometrics, publications 2018–2026, funded projects, RAFT group, teaching, students, media — plus the practical state of Google Scholar / ORCID / OpenAlex / Crossref as machine-readable data sources for the new site.
key_findings: IDENTITY: Canonical name is 'Satish Kumar Regonda'. IITH's institutional profile (https://iith.ac.in/ce/satishr/) uses the full form; Google Scholar, his own Google Site, and most bylines use 'Satish Regonda' / 'S.K. Regonda'. OpenAlex records five display-name variants: 'S. Regonda', 'Satish K Regonda', 'Satish K. Regonda', 'Satish Kumar Regonda', 'Satish Regonda'. One Crossref record (Acta Geophysica, 10.1007/s11600-023-01078-5) has the author name MISSPELLED as 'Satish Khumar Regonda' — which is exactly why OpenAlex does not link that paper to his author ID. A publications page built on automated DOI ingestion will silently drop it.

GOOGLE SCHOLAR (fetched 2026-09-04, https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=cTXdUlUAAAAJ): Citations 1,859 all-time / 587 since 2021; h-index 15 / 12; i10-index 20 / 15. Listed interests: Urban Climate, Urban Floods, Riverine Floods, Hydrologic Modeling, Statistics. Co-authors panel is EMPTY ('No co-authors'), so a Scholar-scraped co-author graph is not available.

TOP 10 MOST-CITED (Google Scholar, verified): (1) Seasonal cycle shifts in hydroclimatology over the western United States, J. Climate 18(2) 372–384, 2005 — 709; (2) The science of NOAA's operational hydrologic ensemble forecast service, BAMS 95(1) 79–98, 2014 — 332; (3) A multimodel ensemble forecast framework: Gunnison River Basin, WRR 42(9), 2006 — 184; (4) Local polynomial method for ensemble forecast of time series, NPG 12(3) 397–406, 2005 — 82; (5) Temporal scaling in river flow: can it be chaotic?, HSJ 49(3) 373–385, 2004 — 71; (6) Short-term ensemble streamflow forecasting (HMOS), J. Hydrology 497 80–96, 2013 — 70; (7) HEFS verification Part 1, J. Hydrology 519 2869–2889, 2014 — 57; (8) HEFS verification Part 2, J. Hydrology 519 2847–2868, 2014 — 52; (9) A new method to produce categorical streamflow forecasts, WRR 42(9), 2006 — 50; (10) Two-dimensional flood inundation modeling in the Godavari River Basin, Water 13(2) 191, 2021 — 38 (his highest-cited India-based paper).

ORCID iD 0000-0003-3188-9415 is REAL and public (verified via https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/0000-0003-3188-9415/record, HTTP 200) but is badly under-populated: no biography, no keywords, no researcher URLs, no education entries, no funding entries, one employment entry ('Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad') with NO start/end dates, and only 14 works — all pre-2022 except three 2021 MDPI papers. It is unusable as a live publications feed today. Fixing it is a ~1-hour job that would give the site a free, stable, CORS-friendly JSON API.

OPENALEX is the single best free machine-readable source for him: author ID A5015401267 (https://api.openalex.org/authors/A5015401267). 55 works, 1,470 citations, h-index 13, i10 18. Filtering works from 2018 returns 34 records with DOIs, full author lists, journal, volume/issue/pages, OA status and citation counts — no API key, no rate-limit pain. Its affiliation history independently corroborates his CV: World Bank (2016), Johns Hopkins University (2016), CIRES (2005, 2006, 2011), University of Colorado Boulder (2005, 2006, 2011), NOAA National Weather Service (2011, 2013, 2014), Riverside Technology Inc. USA (2013, 2014).

CROSSREF is NOT viable as his publication feed: filtering api.crossref.org by his ORCID returns only 5 works (2021 x3, 2025, 2026), because most publishers never deposited his ORCID at submission time.

SEMANTIC SCHOLAR author ID 98921407 (https://www.semanticscholar.org/author/98921407): 44 papers, 1,338 citations, h-index 12. Verified as the same person by DOI lookup on both a 2005 paper (10.1175/JCLI-3272.1) and a 2026 paper (10.1029/2025WR042621) — both resolve to authorId 98921407. Its API is free but aggressively rate-limits unauthenticated calls (I hit HTTP 429 repeatedly).

GOOGLE SCHOLAR HAS NO OFFICIAL API and no plans for one. Practical options, all verified: (a) SerpApi's Google Scholar Author API — https://serpapi.com/google-scholar-author-api — paid, takes author_id=cTXdUlUAAAAJ, returns articles + cited_by table + co-authors, supports sort=pubdate and num up to 100; (b) the Python `scholarly` package — https://pypi.org/project/scholarly/, v1.7.11 (Jan 2023, effectively unmaintained), whose own docs warn that certain queries 'will lead to Google Scholar blocking your requests and may eventually block your IP address' and that proxies are mandatory; (c) manual BibTeX export from the Scholar UI. For a static site the correct answer is NOT to scrape Scholar at all — use OpenAlex for the list and show hand-maintained Scholar metrics with an 'as of <date>' stamp.

EDUCATION (verified verbatim from https://sites.google.com/iith.ac.in/satishregonda/education-employment): Ph.D. University of Colorado at Boulder, Sept 2006, thesis 'Intra-annual to Inter-decadal variability in the Upper Colorado Hydroclimatology: Diagnosis, Forecasting and implications for Water Resources Management'; M.Tech. IIT KANPUR, Aug 2002, thesis 'Investigation of Chaotic behavior in the Hydrologic Time series'; B.Tech. Kakatiya Institute of Technology and Sciences, WARANGAL, June 2000, project 'Computerized Stochastic Modeling of Annual Stream Flow of River Krishna'. IMPORTANT CORRECTIONS to the brief's assumptions: it is IIT KANPUR, not IIT Bombay; it is KITS Warangal, not Osmania University.

EMPLOYMENT (verified verbatim, same page): Associate Professor, CE, IITH (Sept 2022–present); Chairperson, Rural Development Center, IITH (Oct 2023–July 2026 — i.e. this term has now ENDED as of Sept 2026); Assistant Professor, CE, IITH (Feb 2017–Aug 2022); Head, Department of Climate Change, IITH (April 2019–April 2022); Associate Research Scientist, Dept. of Earth & Planetary Sciences, Johns Hopkins University (Mar 2015–Dec 2016); Hydroclimate Consultant, World Bank, Washington DC (May 2014–Dec 2016); Research Hydrologist, Office of Hydrologic Development, NWS/NOAA (Oct 2007–Nov 2013); Postdoctoral Research Associate, National Research Council / NOAA (Oct 2006–Oct 2007). NOTE: his own CV does NOT list Riverside Technology or the NOAA Colorado Basin River Forecast Center — but OpenAlex shows 'Riverside Technology (United States)' as a paper affiliation in 2013–2014, consistent with the common NOAA-OHD contractor arrangement. CBRFC is NOT corroborated anywhere; treat as false unless he confirms.

RAFT = 'Rainfall-runoff Analysis modelling and Forecasting Tools' (his own RAFT page and Deccan Chronicle, 6 Oct 2023). The Google Play listing for SnapFlood uses a slightly different expansion, 'Rainfall-runoff Analysis and Forecasting Tools' (no 'modelling') — pick one canonical expansion for the new site. Stated goal: 'a flood information system for both cities and riverine areas' enabling collaboration among scientists, engineers, policymakers and citizens to build flood-resilient communities. Current roster on his site: PhD — Surya Kiran, Padmini, Saipriya, Lagnajeet, Mohan, Vamshi; MTech — Swagatam, Kanishka, Shruti.

raftwaters.in DOES NOT RESOLVE (curl: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND / exit 000, checked 2026-09-04). satishregonda.in and www.satishregonda.in ALSO DO NOT RESOLVE. Both domains are purchased but have no DNS/hosting configured yet. Do not build a hard link to raftwaters.in that 404s on launch — gate it behind a config flag or link to the on-site RAFT page until DNS is live.

FUNDED PROJECTS (verified): (1) BrahmaSATARK — 'A real-time impact-based 2D flood forecasting system for the Brahmaputra River basin using hydrologic-hydrodynamic and statistical-dynamical approaches', collaboration of IIT Delhi, IIT Gandhinagar, IIT Guwahati, University of Colorado Boulder — listed on https://cc.iith.ac.in/research.html; his own site attributes funding to Monsoon Mission, India. (2) 'Experimental Operational Hydrologic Modeling and Forecasting System for River Basin Hydrology and Extremes for India' — Monsoon Mission / IITM / ESSO / Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), with CU Boulder and IIT Gandhinagar. (3) 'Urban Flood Modeling — A Web-based decision tool' — DST SPLICE Climate Change Programme, IITH + IIT Bhubaneswar. (4) APN project CRRP2018-06MY-Yanto, 'Understanding space-time variability of climate extremes for societal resiliency in Indonesia and India', Asia-Pacific Network for Global Change Research, 2-year project started 2018 (IITH page says 2019–2020); PI Yanto (Jenderal Soedirman Univ.), co-Is Balaji Rajagopalan (CU Boulder), Satish Regonda (IITH), Suroso, Bambang Putra — verified at https://www.apn-gcr.org/project/understanding-space-time-variability-of-climate-extremes-for-societal-resiliency-in-indonesia-and-india/. (5) SnapFlood's Play Store description names two further funders: 'DST-SPLICE, Climate Change Programme, National Network Programme on Urban Climate (NUC), under the National Mission on Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change (NMSKCC)' and 'the Government of India's AI CoE for Sustainable Cities project'. (6) An open CSR fundraising ask, 'A Real-time Urban Flood Information System for the city Hyderabad', PI Regonda, Rs 25,00,000 over 3 years to 31 Dec 2026 — https://giving.iith.ac.in/csr/a_real-time_urban_flood_information_system_for_the_city_hyderabad

PRODUCTS: three live R/Shiny tools (all HTTP 200 on 2026-09-04) — Extreme Climate Analysis Tool for Serayu & Krishna basins (https://satishregondaiith.shinyapps.io/ExtremeClimateAnalysis_Serayu_Krishna_RiverBasins/), Hydro-EMOS streamflow forecast diagnostic/post-processing tool (https://satishregonda.shinyapps.io/HydroEMOS/), Poverty Visualization and Analysis Tool (https://satishregonda.shinyapps.io/PvrtyAppV03/). Plus the SnapFlood Android app (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.snapflood), 100+ downloads, last updated Jul 26 2026, developer contact satishr@ce.iith.ac.in, developer display name oddly reads 'Suresh Regonda' (a typo in the Play Console account). SnapFlood has a mascot named 'VarshaMitra'. Also 'Sixer Tweet' — a Twitter/X-based flood reporting scheme pointing at the account @UFloods83362 (live).

TEACHING (10 courses listed on his site, NO course codes, semesters or UG/PG tags anywhere): Engineering Hydrology; Open Channel Hydraulics; Fundamentals of RS & GIS; RS & GIS Lab; Fluid Mechanics Lab; Engineering Hydrology and Hydrologic Systems; Applied Computational Laboratory; Hydraulic and Hydrologic Simulation Lab; Climate Monitoring and Variability; RS, GIS and Climate Change.

STUDENT PIPELINE is substantial and is the single richest, most 'human' content he already maintains: 6 graduated PhDs (Vimal Chandra Sharma 2021, Dagani Koteswara Rao 2022, Mohammed Azharuddin 2024, Ponukumati Adilakshmi Padmini 2025, Guniganti Surya Kiran 2026, Vaishnavi B 2026 co-supervised), 9 current PhD scholars, 2 current MTech, 9 graduated MTech, 3 UG mini-project students — all with thesis topics and dates on https://sites.google.com/iith.ac.in/satishregonda/students. Critically, NO alumni current-position data is recorded; that is the obvious first content gap to fill in the new Google Sheet.

MEDIA: two verified national outlets, both Oct 2023 and both about UFIS/SnapFlood — Deccan Chronicle, 6 Oct 2023 (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/in-other-news/061023/innovative-urban-flood-information-system-aims-to-transform-citys-res.html), which names supporting agencies GHMC, IMD, TSDPS, Irrigation Department and CWC; and The Hans India, 5 Oct 2023 (https://www.thehansindia.com/hans/education-careers/iith-initiates-a-groundbreaking-endeavor-to-tackle-persistent-issue-of-urban-flooding-in-hyderabad-827649). Plus an IITH YouTube video 'Urban Flood Information System by Raft Group' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zz9i62ucZ3c) and an IITH Facebook video (https://www.facebook.com/iithyderabad/videos/879817213573116/, HTTP 200). He has also delivered NIDM (National Institute of Disaster Management) training sessions on UFIS — report PDFs exist at nidm.gov.in for Nov 2024 and May 2025, but the PDFs are image-scanned and I could not extract their text directly; the Regonda attribution comes from search-engine indexing of those PDFs, so treat the exact session titles as UNVERIFIED.

CONTACT DATA IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS OFFICIAL PAGES — this needs resolving before launch. Phone: iith.ac.in/ce/satishr/ says (040) 2359-6315; civil.iith.ac.in/people/faculty and his own Google Site say +91 40 2301-6315. PIN code: iith.ac.in says Kandi-502284; the CE dept and his site say 502285. Email is obfuscated on his site as both 'satishr.at.iith.ac.in' (home) and 'satishr.at.ce.iith.ac.in' (opportunities); the department listing gives the canonical satishr@ce.iith.ac.in. Office: Room B-212, Dept. of Civil Engineering.
recommendations: Do NOT scrape Google Scholar from the site — no official API, `scholarly` is unmaintained and warns of IP bans, and SerpApi is a paid dependency the professor cannot maintain. Instead: build the publications list from OpenAlex (author A5015401267) as a BUILD-TIME fetch baked into the static output, and render the three Scholar headline numbers (1,859 citations / h-index 15 / i10-index 20) as hand-entered values in the Google Sheet with a visible 'as of <month year>' stamp. A stale number with a date is honest; a broken scraper is not.

Make the Google Sheet the source of truth for publications, NOT OpenAlex alone. OpenAlex misses the Acta Geophysica 2023 paper purely because of the 'Khumar' typo at Crossref, and it mixes 20+ AGU/EGU abstracts and ESSOAr preprints in with journal articles. Structure the sheet with an explicit `type` column (journal | book-chapter | conference | preprint | thesis) and a `featured` boolean so he can curate; seed it with the ~21 peer-reviewed 2018–2026 items in the details section below, each with its DOI already filled in.

Fix his ORCID record as a one-off task and then link it prominently. It currently has 14 works, no bio, no education, and one undated employment entry. Once populated it becomes a free, stable, CORS-friendly JSON endpoint (https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/0000-0003-3188-9415/record) and — more valuable for him personally — the canonical identity that publishers auto-populate going forward. This is a genuine deliverable to offer him, not just site plumbing.

Do not hard-link raftwaters.in in the initial launch. It does not resolve as of 2026-09-04 (nor does satishregonda.in). Put the RAFT link behind a single config constant so it can be switched on the day DNS goes live, and until then point 'RAFT research team →' at the on-site RAFT page.

Anchor the site's identity on ONE distinctive fact rather than the generic 'hydrology professor' framing: he is an operational forecaster who came back. He spent 2006–2013 building NOAA's national Hydrologic Ensemble Forecast Service (the BAMS paper, 332 citations) and now runs a citizen-science flood app for Hyderabad with 100+ installs. That arc — US federal operational forecasting → Indian urban flooding, national scale → one city — is the editorial spine. Nothing about it reads as a template.

Give SnapFlood and the three Shiny tools a real 'Tools' or 'Products' section with live status, not a buried link list. All four URLs return HTTP 200 today. These are the only things on his current site a non-academic visitor (a GHMC official, a journalist) can actually click and use, and they are completely lost in the current Google Sites layout.

Structure the students content as two Sheet tabs, `students_current` and `students_alumni`, with columns name / degree / start / graduated / thesis_title / current_position / photo_url. He already maintains 29 student records with thesis topics and dates; the only missing field is `current_position`, which is the single highest-value thing he can add and the thing prospective PhD applicants most want to see.

Resolve the phone/PIN/email inconsistencies with him directly before launch and then make the new site the canonical record: satishr@ce.iith.ac.in, Room B-212, Dept. of Civil Engineering, IIT Hyderabad, Kandi, Sangareddy, Telangana 502285. Ask him to confirm which phone number actually reaches him.

Pick and freeze one RAFT expansion. His site and the press say 'Rainfall-runoff Analysis modelling and Forecasting Tools'; the Play Store says 'Rainfall-runoff Analysis and Forecasting Tools'. Use the former (it matches the press coverage and his own page) and update the Play Store copy to match.

Seed the blog with content he demonstrably already produces rather than asking him to write from scratch: NIDM training sessions, AGU session convening (he organised session H111, 'Understanding, Modeling, Forecasting and Mitigation of Urban and Riverine Flood Risks in South Asia', AGU Fall 2021), the Indonesia/APN collaboration, and the Hyderabad 2020/2021 flood case studies. A first post drawn from his existing NIDM slides is a much easier ask than a blank page.

Add an 'Openings' page driven from the Sheet — he already has a written, specific ask on his current site (email subject line 'Looking for an Opportunity', with four required bullet points). Reproducing that verbatim, well-typeset, will measurably improve his applicant quality and costs nothing.

Explicitly ASK him for the items I could not verify anywhere public: awards/honours, editorial board or associate editor roles, reviewer service, professional memberships (AGU/AMS/IAHS/ISH?), Scopus author ID confirmation, Web of Science ResearcherID, ResearchGate and LinkedIn URLs he wants linked, and whether he has a GitHub. None of these exist in any fetchable public source — an academic site with an empty 'Awards' section looks worse than one that omits the section, so decide per-section based on his answers.
pitfalls: Auto-generating the publications page from Crossref-by-ORCID would show only 5 papers. Auto-generating from OpenAlex alone would silently drop the Acta Geophysica 2023 paper (author-name typo 'Khumar' at the publisher) and would pad the list with 20+ AGU/EGU abstracts and ESSOAr preprints presented as if they were journal articles. Either failure makes a senior academic look less productive than he is — the most damaging possible error on this site.

Scraping Google Scholar at runtime will get the site's IP blocked and the publications page will start rendering empty or throwing. The `scholarly` docs say this outright. A static site that quietly breaks six months after handover is worse than no automation.

Year metadata genuinely disagrees between sources — his own site, OpenAlex and Google Scholar assign different years to the SAME paper (e.g. the J. Hydrology 132407 paper is 2024 on his site and OpenAlex but 2025 on Scholar; the JWRPM WRENG-5644 paper is 2023 on his site, 2022 in OpenAlex, issue-dated 2023). Pick ONE authority (I recommend the journal's issue year, as printed on his own site) and state the rule, or the year headings will look sloppy.

Do not state that he worked at the NOAA Colorado Basin River Forecast Center. Nothing anywhere corroborates it. His NOAA role was Research Hydrologist at the Office of Hydrologic Development (NWS HQ, Silver Spring/Washington DC area). Similarly, do not write 'IIT Bombay' or 'Osmania University' — it is IIT Kanpur (M.Tech) and KITS Warangal (B.Tech).

Do not describe him as Head of the Department of Climate Change in the present tense. He held that role April 2019–April 2022; cc.iith.ac.in currently lists Dr. Asif Qureshi as HoD. Likewise his Rural Development Center chairpersonship is listed as ending July 2026, which is now past — confirm before publishing it as current.

The professor's editing workflow will break if the Sheet schema requires him to hand-type DOIs or BibTeX. Pre-fill every existing row; make the only required fields for a NEW row the ones he can copy off an acceptance email (authors, title, journal, year, DOI). Never make him touch a URL slug, a date format, or a boolean spelled TRUE/FALSE.

Publishing the students table with an empty `current_position` column for 15+ alumni will read as neglect. Either populate it (he likely knows most of them) or design the component to gracefully omit the column until it has data.

Reproducing the current Google Sites information architecture 1:1 will reproduce its central flaw: 'Products & Publications' currently mixes three Shiny apps, 22 journal papers, 2 book chapters, ~17 years of conference abstracts, invited seminars and 'scientific activities' into one endless scrolling page. That page needs to become at least three distinct destinations.

His ORCID, Scopus, ResearchGate and LinkedIn are all findable but three of the four are either unpopulated or unfetchable. Do not render a row of six identical profile-badge icons — an academic site whose ORCID badge leads to a near-empty record actively undermines credibility. Link only the profiles that are actually worth landing on (Google Scholar today; ORCID once fixed).

Returns articles, citation counts, cited-by table, co-authors. Reliable but introduces a recurring cost and a key the professor cannot rotate. |
| **`scholarly` (Python)** | https://pypi.org/project/scholarly/ | Free, **v1.7.11 released Jan 2023** — effectively unmaintained. Its own docs: *"Making certain types of queries, such as `scholarly.citedby` or `scholarly.search_pubs`, will lead to Google Scholar blocking your requests and may eventually block your IP address."* Proxies are mandatory; Tor support deprecated since 1.5. **Not appropriate for a site he must maintain.** |
| **Manual BibTeX export** | Scholar UI → select all → Export → BibTeX | Zero dependency, always works, but is a manual step. |
| **OpenAlex (recommended)** | https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=author.id:A5015401267 | Free, no key, no rate-limit issues, full metadata incl. DOI/volume/pages/OA status. Missing only the "Khumar" paper. |

**Recommended architecture:** build-time fetch from OpenAlex → merged with a curated Google Sheet (which wins on conflicts and supplies the missing/typo'd records) → static JSON baked into the site. Scholar's three headline numbers entered by hand in the Sheet with an "as of" date.
